Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:163: Now, our holy Torah explained to us these two aspects mentioned for the acquisition of holiness at the beginning of Parashat Kedoshim - when it wished to explain how we cleave to Him and His holiness rests upon us, saying (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy," and so on, it began to explain the stages of acquiring holiness, saying, "every man, you shall fear your mother and your father" - and it is known that his father and mother are the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, as explained in the Zohar several times (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 77a) - and it put the mother first, since the essential fear is toward her, as explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 14, and it said "your mother and your father," not "you shall fear your mother and your father," to indicate that it is fitting to fear one's mother in her capacity as mother and one's father in his capacity as father - meaning that they bore him and did good for him, and it is fitting that he not vex them and transgress their will and be ungrateful, Heaven forfend.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:164: "And you shall keep My Sabbaths" - we have already explained above that the Sabbath is a repair for the days of the week, for on the Sabbath day one receives flow and illumination, and one must, during the six weekdays, repair his deeds so that he can receive the soul that comes on the Sabbath day, which is from Atzilut - it follows that the six weekdays are found between two Sabbaths, going out from Sabbath and entering into Sabbath, and this order was even present in the creation of the world, as my teacher explained in Sefer HaPardes. And to this our Rabbis, of blessed memory, may have intended (cf. Shabbat 118b), in saying, "had Israel kept two Sabbaths, no nation would have ruled over them" - and to this, "and you shall keep My Sabbaths" - and the plural, "Sabbaths," refers to the six days in between, as explained above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:165: "I am the LORD your God" - this is the bond of the supernal holiness within us, resting upon us through the repair mentioned - for through fear one draws the Shechinah upon himself, since she is called "fear," and in her all of Atzilut dwells, and according to how a person prepares himself for fear, so holiness dwells upon him, as explained in the teaching from Parashat Yitro. And likewise the acquisition of the supernal soul through the repair of the six days is certainly a repair for the Shechinah to rest in him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:166: And corresponding to the aspect of fear explained, King David, peace be upon him, said to his son Solomon (1 Chronicles 28:9), "and you, Solomon my son, know the God of your father, and serve Him with a whole heart and a willing soul, for the LORD searches all hearts, and understands every inclination of the thoughts; if you seek Him, He will be found by you, but if you forsake Him, He will cast you off forever." And this verse, as a whole, reveals to us all the aspects we have explained. First it says, "know the God of your father" - and this knowledge is to know whom he serves, that He is the Cause over all, the root and source of all worlds, as explained - and this is "the God of your father," which indicates providence. And by way of secret, "the God of your father" - through the final measure the supernal Godhead is revealed to the lower beings, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:167: "And serve Him with a whole heart" - the intent is along the lines of "and you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart" (Deuteronomy 6:5), with the good inclination and with the evil inclination (Berachot, chapter 9, mishnah 5), since both rest in the heart, in the two chambers of the heart, as explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 5 - and when the evil inclination, resting in the heart on the left side, is subdued beneath the good inclination, then it is a "whole heart," for the two hearts become one heart; but if the good inclination wishes to direct itself to holiness and the evil inclination accuses it, they are two separate hearts, and it is not wholeness. And it is possible to explain this by way of secret, but we do not wish to depart from our discourse.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:168: "And a willing soul" - shall be explained to you by what is explained in the Gate of Love, chapter 4, concerning "for he desired [chafetz] Jacob's daughter" (Genesis 34:19), where the matter of "the desire of the heart" is explained, which is the complete longing following divine service. "And every inclination of the thoughts understands" - explained by our Rabbis, of blessed memory, and we copied their wording in the Gate of Love, chapter 8.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:169: "If you seek Him, He will be found by you" - here it teaches what we explained from the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him (Parashat Yitro, page 69a), that whoever wishes to draw a spirit from above needs fear and a broken heart, and so on, as explained - and this is "if you seek Him," for seeking is needed until "He will be found by you," and this is along the lines of (Deuteronomy 13:15), "then you shall inquire, and search," and likewise (Leviticus 10:16), "Moses diligently sought" - since it does not say "if you find Him, He will be found by you." And it is possible that "seeking" is explained as Radak explains in Sefer HaShorashim, that it means readiness, along the lines of (Isaiah 65:1), "I was sought by those who did not ask" - the intent being, I was found and made ready - and likewise (Psalms 111:2), "sought out by all who desire them" - ready and found, and so on. And so, when a person makes himself ready and prepares himself to receive holiness, the Holy One, blessed be He, will be found by him - but if he does not prepare himself properly, the Holy One, blessed be He, will not be found by him. And from saying "He will be found" and not "He will seek you," it teaches what they said (Yoma 39a), "whoever comes to purify himself is assisted," for being "found" is more significant than "seeking." And in saying "by you" [lach], the explanation is that from your side it is needed that He be found by you, but He, of Himself, is [always] found.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:170: "But if you forsake Him, He will cast you off forever" - and this is along the lines of what they said, of blessed memory (Jerusalem Talmud, end of Berachot; Midrash Shmuel 1): "if you forsake Me one day, I will forsake you two days" - a parable of two friends who were near each other; one turned to his path, a day's journey eastward, and the other also turned to his path, a day's journey westward - it is found that between them is a two-day journey - and this is "two days I will forsake you," and this is "He will cast you off forever." And further, "He will cast you off forever" may mean that he will not be among the members of the supernal household called "servants of the LORD," as explained in the Zohar - the reason being that only those forever bound in thought ascend there, as explained in chapter 4. And therefore a person, when he begins to grasp holiness and cleave to his Maker one day, should follow it with another day, since it will be twice as much toil to find the cleaving he had, as they said, of blessed memory, "if he forgets, he shall surely forget" (Deuteronomy 8:19) - if a person forgets a little, they cause him to forget much - and this is his saying "if you forsake Him," even a slight forsaking, and it does not say "if you cast Him off" - and this is "He will cast you off forever," for the reason stated, which is along the lines of "if you forsake Me one day," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:171: Further, among the things that cause the holiness of thoughts, King Solomon, peace be upon him, revealed to us in saying (Proverbs 16:3), "commit your works to the LORD, and your thoughts shall be established" - and the intent is several matters, all relevant to the holiness of thought.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:172: The first, according to its plain sense, is along the lines of (Psalms 55:23), "cast your burden upon the LORD" - and they explained in the Talmud (Rosh Hashanah 26b) that "yehavcha" [your burden] means a load, and the intent is the load of worldly matters, such as a person's supporting his household and his livelihood and his business dealings - that he should cast them upon the LORD, in whose hand it is to arrange everything, for all these matters confuse a person's thought. And to this it says, "commit your works to the LORD," and through this "your thoughts shall be established" - and this is a virtue among the qualities of trust, as elaborated in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Trust, introduction), that it is the rest of the soul from the mishaps of the world and from traveling roads and the like, trusting in his Master that his livelihood will not fail him, as it is said (Psalms 23:1), "the LORD is my shepherd, I shall not want" - for YHVH, who created him, knows his affairs, for his good, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 131:2), "like a weaned child with its mother." And when a person strengthens himself in trust in Him, blessed be He, it will be a great cause for the purification of thought, for since he casts all his matters upon the LORD, he has no other thought but that very thing he is occupied with, prayer or Torah or a commandment - all of it for divine service without any ulterior motive.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:173: This is the plain sense of the verse. It means, "commit your works to the LORD" refers to the health of the limbs of his body, along the lines of (Deuteronomy 32:6), "He made you and established you," as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Bereshit Rabbah 12:1), that the Holy One, blessed be He, and His court took a census over every limb, and so on. And "commit to the LORD" means that although a person's limbs and body are physical, when he commits them and binds them to their root, which is YHVH, the limbs shall be refined and the thoughts established. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained this matter in several ways, that YHVH is found alluded to in the limbs of a person - they said in the Tikkunim (page 131b), in these words: YHVH is found in every single limb - He is found in the four colors of the hair, and in the four colors of the eye, and in the four folds of the ear, and in the four colors of the face, and in voice, and in speech, and in reading, and in saying, and in the actions of the hands, and in every single limb of the body He is YHVH, and so on - to this point, relevant here. The rest of his wording we copied in the Gate of Fear.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:174: Further, they explained in the Tikkunim that the Name YHVH is found in a person's body: Yud in the head, Heh-Heh in the hands, Vav in the body. This is his wording (page 128b): come and see, He [Yud] is the head, and He is the measure of the eyes, of the ears, of the face, of the two nostrils of the nose, a measure in the mouth - "a just weight" (Leviticus 19:36), this is Vav, the weight of the body, the wings of the scale are Heh, the five fingers of the right and the five of the left - and because the Name YHVH is measure, size, and weight, the verse says, "you shall not commit injustice in judgment, in measure, in weight, or in volume" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:175: Further, they explained in the Tikkunim (page 68b) that the full Name spelled with alefs, Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud [wait, this should be the alef-spelling], is found alluded to in the limbs of the human body, in these words: and therefore the right leg, which has three joints, is bound with the right arm, in which the Heh rests; and likewise the left arm with the left leg, in which the Heh rests; and likewise the body and the covenant are Vav-Vav, and in them rests the Alef, which is Imma, and becomes "Yud-Gimel Vav" [thirteen and six, i.e., YHVH's numerology]. Yud rests in the ten fingers of the hands and the ten toes of the feet, because the beginning of the holy Name rests from Chokhmah, which is in the fingers; the supernal Crown rests in the head of a person, where sealed thought is, and just as thought is sealed, so it [the head] is sealed - to this point. And he says further there, the four foundations of the body, in them YHVH rests - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:176: And further, in the Tikkunim, in manuscript (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 114b), that every single limb of a person comprises ten, alluding to the Name Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud, and concerning it is said (Genesis 1:26), "let us make man" - for "Adam" is nine in the small reckoning [gematria katanah], and the Shechinah is "the image of man," completing the tenth aspect in every single limb. And at the end of his words he says, this is the lower Shechinah, the completion of the higher and lower beings, and so it goes in every single limb and in every single sefirah, and it says "let us make man" until the Shechinah is included in all the sefirot and in every limb, at the time all the limbs were completed in her, each one to ten, in this manner, Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud - afterward it descends to four, and so on - this requires study there - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:177: And after setting forth the knowledge of these teachings, the verse shall be explained in two aspects, both relevant to practice. The first, "commit your works to the LORD," is that after he knows that all his limbs, which are called "works" [ma'asim], as explained, are sealed with the Name YHVH, he must not sin with them, as Scripture says (Leviticus 19:35), "you shall not commit injustice in judgment, in measure, in weight, or in volume," and it explains that these four measures correspond to the Name YHVH: judgment - Yud, measure - Heh, weight - Vav, volume - Heh. And Rashbi, peace be upon him, said, before the teaching we copied (Tikkunim, page 128b): and therefore, "you shall not commit injustice in judgment, in measure," and so on - "measure" here is the measure of the stature [shi'ur komah], for whoever does not possess [good] measures diminishes the supernal stature and is not raised from there, for the ten supernal sefirot all go by measure from the side of the letter Yud, and by weight from the side of the letter Vav; the two pans of the scale are Heh-Heh - to this point. And once the limbs are clean and are a throne for YHVH, the thoughts shall be established, as explained above in chapter 6, that the supernal thought rests only on a complete and properly repaired throne.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:178: And so, when he considers that the brains in his head hold an allusion to the Name YHVH, four brains corresponding to the Name YHVH, corresponding to the four passages in the tefillin, which are called the Name YHVH, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Mishpatim, page 119b), it is fitting that he purify his thoughts - and this is included in "commit your works to the LORD," which explains that the Name YHVH is alluded to in every single limb of a person, and particularly in the four brains it is alluded to more.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:179: And further, this matter is explained at greater length - Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained there (page 130a) four aspects: sight, hearing, smell, speech. And he says afterward, there is no repair from these four letters that does not include the ten sefirot, which are Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud, and the four letters that are YHVH - He does not change in any place: He hears to the left, toward Israel, and looks to the right upon them, and in the south He hovers over them - this is what is written (Genesis 1:2), "and the spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters" - and in the west He speaks with them. They [the aspects] change in the vessels of the body, but in Him there is no change at all - this is what is written (Malachi 3:6), "I the LORD do not change" - and every single limb, which is the candle of every precept, a person must consult the Holy One, blessed be He, and prepare for it a clean and pure place to rest there - and therefore a person must remove from every single limb all thoughts and all evil, filthy reflections, which are husks, and must illuminate them with all the precepts that rest upon every single limb, which are candles, for every precept is called a candle, this is what is written (Proverbs 6:23), "for the commandment is a candle" - "the candle of the LORD is the soul of man" (ibid. 20:27) - to this point, relevant here. And what it says, "He hears to the left," and so on, "and in the west He speaks," and so on, is explained earlier in this teaching, and is not relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:180: And what emerges from the general sense of the teaching is that a person must repair all his limbs so that they be a throne on which the Name YHVH rests, which is the soul resting within - and any blemish in any limb causes the Name YHVH to withdraw, as explained further there, and we copied the whole teaching in the Gate of Fear, chapter 9 - see there. And this is "commit your works to the LORD," as explained, "and your thoughts shall be established" - meaning the name of thought, Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud, which is the inner soul that spreads through the limbs.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:181: And especially in light of what is explained above in the teaching of Rashbi, peace be upon him, from the end of Tikkun 22 (page 68b), that the name of thought, Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud, is alluded to in the limbs of a person - one might say "commit to YHVH" plainly, and the intent is, commit to this Name your works, the limbs alluded to in this Name, "and your thoughts shall be established," for once the limbs are purified so that the Name rests upon them, the thoughts shall be established, for this Name is bound with thought, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 7:182: And with this the chapter is concluded:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:1: We have already explained in chapter 7, in the name of Rashbi, that the brain's chariot has four [aspects]: sight, hearing, smell, speech - and he said in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 234a) that these four correspond to the four letters of YHVH, saying: the brain has four living creatures, which are the throne of mercy - and what are they? Sight, hearing, smell, speech. Sight - lion; hearing - ox; smell - eagle - and four faces and four wings for each one. Speech - man, which holds above and below - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:2: Now, after we have explained in the previous chapters the holiness of the brain and heart, both bound together concerning reflection, as we explained, let us now come, in this chapter, to explain what is relevant to the holiness of sight. And we begin to explain the matter of sight after having explained the holiness of the heart, because they are adjacent and dependent on each other - "the heart and the eye are two brokers of sin" (Yalkut, part 1, remez 750), as we explained. Concerning the particulars of the eye, we shall copy everything found in the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, who explains the particulars of the eye - and when a person knows the place of the allusion in the supernal chariot, he shall sanctify his sight properly.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:3: Concerning the three colors of the eye, the pupil, and the eyelids, he explained in Tikkun 4 (page 18b), in these words: "In the beginning" - it is written (Psalms 118:19), "open for me the gates of righteousness; I will enter them, I will give thanks to the LORD." "Open for me" certainly refers to the two eyelids, which open and close, and concerning them it is said (Exodus 25:20), "and the cherubim shall spread their wings above" - these cherubim are the two cherubim of the eye, "spreading wings" are the eyelids of the eye. And further, "open for me the gates of righteousness" are the two eyes - at the time they are on the straight path, of them it is said (ibid.), "and their faces one toward another"; and at the time they do not look on the straight path, behold the twisted serpent is there, of which it is said (Ruth 1:17), "for death shall separate." The three colors of the eye are the three Patriarchs, of whom it is said (Exodus 6:14), "these are the heads of their fathers' houses." The pupil, which is small and tiny, is the Shechinah who joins in the limbs, and concerning her it is said (Psalms 17:8), "guard me as the pupil, the daughter of the eye" - and all is in the secret of "Bereshit" [In the beginning] - there "roshei" [heads], there "bat" [daughter] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:4: The two eyelids that open and close, they explained (Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Ki Teitzei, page 280b), are Netzach and Hod. And what he said, "cherubim of the eye" and "eyelids of the eye," is explained in the Tikkunim (page 128a), in these words: and further, the eye is like the body - its two cherubim are like the two legs, and the two eyelids of the eye correspond to the two arms; these shield and those fly - to this point. And it appears that the lower "wings" of the eyes are what are called cherubim, and the eyelids are the upper ones that shield the eye.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:5: And concerning the pupil, he says in the Tikkunim (end of page 51a) that the pupil is the daughter of "Bereshit," comprising ten utterances - she is the black pupil, of whom it is said (Song of Songs 1:5), "I am black, but comely," and in her light shines - this is what is written (Proverbs 6:23), "and Torah is light" - to this point, in brief.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:6: And in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Ki Teitzei, page 280b) they explained how the Name YHVH is found in the eye, and they said, in these words: the holy lamp [Rashbi] said to him: Yud is the pupil of the eye, for "the commandment is a candle and the Torah is light"; Heh-Vav shine in it; Heh - the three colors, the appearance of the eye, and the two wings of the eye; five lights shine within it; the supernal Heh, which is light - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:7: Further, in the Tikkunim (end of page 128a), in these words: the eyes, in their roundness, are from the side of the letter Yud; in their length, from the side of the letter Vav; the wings of the eye are Heh-Heh - in these four letters the eye is by measure and by weight - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:8: Further, in the allusion of the particulars of the eye, they explained in the Tikkunim (page 128a), in these words: and further, "and their eyebrows" - these are the seven layers of the eye, one upon another like the layers of onions, and their "eyebrow" is the eye that comprises all the colors, "and their eyebrows full of eyes" [combining Job 16:16, Ezekiel 1:18] - these are the wings of the eye and the eyelids of the eye, for there are four colors in the eye, corresponding to the four faces of every living creature, and the two wings of the eye, which are the eyelids, and the two cherubim of the eye correspond to the four wings of every living creature - and in these four colors of the eye the four letters of YHVH shine, and in the four wings of the eye Adonai shines - this is (Ecclesiastes 5:7), "for one high official watches over another high official," and higher than them are YHVH, Ehyeh, Abba and Imma - to this point. And the intent, in brief, is that in the eyelids and the wings of the eye - two in each eye - correspond to the four wings of the living creatures, which are the Name Adonai; and the four colors correspond to the Name YHVH; and the light that shines in the eyelids is YHVH and Ehyeh, Abba and Imma.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:9: Further, there, right after: the cherubim of the eye and the eyelids of the eye, of them it is said (Exodus 25:20), "and the cherubim shall spread their wings above, covering with their wings over the cover [kapporet]" - this is the covering [kapparah] of the eye. The three colors of the eye are Ehyeh, YHVH, Adonai - general, particular, and general - they are Unity, Blessing, Holiness, with the mnemonic "Ya'aneinu Beyom Koreinu" [may He answer us on the day we call], for these three Names total, in numerical value, "Yabak" [52+26+65=143... a known numerological identity]. Ehyeh is the supernal Crown, YHVH is the central pillar, Adonai is the lower Shechinah - Adonai is general, Ehyeh is particular, YHVH is both general and particular - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:10: Further, they explained in the Tikkunim (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash, page 96b) that in the eye there is both YHVH and Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud, in these words: and some explain them thus, with the ten letters of the Explicit Name: in the seven layers of the eye and the three colors of the eye shine ten letters, which are Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud - and this is "and the likeness of the face of man"; in the two cherubim of the eye and the two eyelids of the eye shine the faces of man, which are four, and they are YHVH, of whom it is said (Ezekiel 1:10), "and the likeness of their faces was the face of a man" - the likeness of three living creatures is the likeness of the faces of man - to this point. And although this is said there concerning the particulars of the eye of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, nevertheless it is possible to learn from it also for ourselves, for Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the Tikkunim (page 130a), whose wording we copied above (chapter 7), that sight, hearing, smell, and speech - in each of them there is YHVH and Yud-Kaf-Yud Vav-Kaf-Yud - and it was not explained there how, but it is possible to understand it from what is explained in this teaching.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:11: And when you examine precisely the Names that Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained concerning the eye, you shall find in the eye the entirety of the whole "stature" [shi'ur komah], particularly in the three Names that total "Yabak," and you already know what the commentators explained, that the pupil is called "ishon" [little man] because the form of a small man is seen in it - and along these lines, the reason for the appearance of the form of a man in it is for the reason stated, that the figure of the whole stature is imprinted and concealed there in the Names mentioned.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:12: And so they further explained there in the Tikkunim (page 128a), in the particulars of the eye, that it holds an allusion to the entirety of the body, as we copied above, where it says, "two cherubim like two legs, two eyelids of the eye corresponding to two arms." And it says further there, corresponding to the wings of the eye are the two lips that open and close, and corresponding to them are the two wings of the lung, and the eye corresponds to the heart, which is a blazing fire, and so on - behold, the allusion of the whole person in the eye.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:13: And further, there is in it an allusion to the whole world, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 226a), that the white surrounding the whole eye is an allusion to the ocean sea that surrounds the whole world, and the second color is the dry land and the waters in it, and the third is Jerusalem, standing in the middle of the world, and the fourth color, which is the pupil, from where the light emerges, is the point of Zion, the Foundation Stone in the Sanctuary of the Holy of Holies, from which the world was founded, and there the Shechinah would rest, and from there her light goes out to the world - and this same matter is explained also in the Tikkunim (page 126b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:14: Let us return to the matter - since the eye holds an allusion to all the holy Names mentioned, and the whole "stature," and the whole world, whoever guards his eyes from sinning with them guards his whole body and sustains the world by his merit - and if, Heaven forfend, he blemishes them, he blemishes all that has been mentioned. And therefore it is fitting that a person not gaze with his eyes upon a place of nakedness - for the general blemish is in the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, since he blemishes the holy sight of Tiferet [glorification], which emerges from the pupil, which is the Shechinah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:15: And even concerning matters that are merely permitted, one should not satiate his eye - for so it is explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna, that any sight that is not of Torah or a commandment, the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah do not rest there, in these words (Zohar, Parashat Pinchas, end of page 229): and sight and hearing where there is no Torah and commandment, the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah do not rest there - for the Holy One, blessed be He, rests in sight, and so His Shechinah, in Torah, "and Torah is light," His Shechinah is His sight, YHVH - "in a vision [mar'ah] I make Myself known to him" - His Shechinah is made known - to this point. The intent is that in sight alone the allusion to the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah is found: the allusion to the Holy One, blessed be He, is that it is called "Torah is light"; the allusion to His Shechinah is that the verse says, "in a vision [mar'ah] I make Myself known to him," and "the vision" is the Shechinah, as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Ki Teitzei, page 280b). And it is possible to say that this is the aspect of the pupil, which is the "vision" that emerges through the supernal light of Tiferet.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:16: And among the repairs of the eyes is what the verse says (Job 22:29), "and He shall save the humble of eyes [shach einayim]," which brings one to shame and humility - and so is the testament of the Ramban to his son: do not look into a person's face while speaking with him. And so they explained in the Midrash, in these words: Rabbi Acha bar Yoshiya said, do not look at women, lest you come to speak of forbidden matters, and the Sages say, whoever has shame of face does not easily sin, as it is said (Exodus 20:17 - actually 20:20), "and so that His fear be upon your faces, that you not sin"; and whoever has no shame of face easily sins, as it is said (Isaiah 3:9), "the look of their faces testifies against them" - to this point. And it must be that shame of face comes from having "humble eyes," for if one has haughty eyes, certainly he has no shame of face - and through this the connection between the words of the Sages and the words of Rabbi Acha bar Yoshiya is understood, for the Sages came to add to his words and said that not only will he not come to speak of forbidden matters, but he will also acquire shame of face - and whoever has this does not easily sin, even a light sin; and whoever has no shame of face, since haughtiness of eyes indicates brazenness of face, easily sins.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:17: And know that for the repair of thought, one must have "humble eyes," and through this he repairs his thought in every aspect - whether by not gazing at women (a woman he has not seen, he will not come to think of her), and even concerning permitted matters, such as colorful garments spread on a wall, as we shall further copy their teaching, of blessed memory (Avodah Zarah 20b) - for anything a person gazes at, that thing and its image are imprinted in his intellect, and it is found that when he comes to pray or occupy himself with Torah, the physical forms of what he saw are imprinted in his intellect, and a blemish and confusion in thought is found, and he cannot direct his intent properly - for the eyes see only by the power of the soul, and it is found that the power of the soul goes outward and absorbs that thing, and it is imaged in the brain of imagination, as we explained in chapter 6, that there are three brains - and if the thing he gazed at was nakedness, he has brought nakedness into a high place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:18: And this was the virtue of our father Abraham, peace be upon him, of whom they said, of blessed memory (Bava Batra 16a), on the verse (Genesis 12:11), "now I know that you are a woman beautiful to look at," that he had never gazed at his own wife - and the reason, as explained, is so as not to send the power of the soul outward and bring a physical thing into his intellect, for this would cause confusion of thought, as explained, and would be found mixing the profane with the holy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:19: And therefore it is fitting for a person, when he wishes to pray, not to look at anyone's face, even a child's, so that he not come to think of that person's affairs - but rather, at the time he prays, he should sanctify himself and think that he has no relation or closeness with any person but with the Creator of his soul alone - and this will be a great aid to intent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 8:20: But a person's gazing at the face of his teacher is a commandment and a repair for the eyes, for through that gazing he acquires for his soul the illumination of the pure soul that shows in his face - especially the greeting of his face on Sabbath and festival - and greeting the face of any sage is a repair for the eyes.
